![
**Figure 2 | Specificity tests of the _Sousa chinensis_ qPCR assay against three sympatric Delphinidae species.** (**a**) Amplification curves of _S. chinensis_ standard DNA across a dilution series ($0$ to $10,000$ copies/µL). Different colors indicate different template concentrations. (**b**–**g**) Amplification curves of synthesized target-region (Cytb) DNA from three non-target, but potentially co-occurring cetacean species (red curves) tested at 100 copies/µL (**b**, **d**, **f**; slightly exceeding the maximum concentration observed in our “proof-of-concept” field samples, ~60 copies/µL) and 1,000 copies/µL (**c**, **e**, **g**), plotted alongside the _S. chinensis_ standard DNA curves (gray curves, $0$ to $10,000$ copies/µL): (**b**, **c**) _Stenella coeruleoalba_, (**d**, **e**) _Delphinus capensis_ and (**f**, **g**) _Tursiops truncatus_. 
](formatted_figs/Fig02_RelatedSppAmp.pdf){width=100%}

</center>


<center>

![
**Figure 3 | Standard curve, the limit of detection (LOD) and limit of quantification (LOQ) of the primers and probe specific to _Sousa chinensis_.** (**a**) Standard curve generated from 24 technical replicates across eight standard DNA concentrations ($1$ to $2.0 \times 10^6$ copies/reaction). The $x$-axis represents copy numbers of the _Cytb_ target region per qPCR reaction, and the $y$-axis represents the $C_{t}$ value. Following Klymus et al. (2020), filled black points indicate data included in the linear regression (the middle two quartiles, i.e., 25th–75th percentiles, of standards with $\ge 50\%$ detection rates), whereas blue "+" symbols indicate data excluded from the regression (points outside the middle two quartiles or standards with $< 50\%$ detection rates, i.e., 1 copy/reaction). The red solid vertical line and black dashed vertical line indicate the modeled LOD (3.22 copies/reaction) and modeled LOQ (14 copies/reaction), respectively. (**b**) Determination of the LOD. Open circles indicate observed detection rates at each standard concentration. The two-parameter Weibull type II model (`W2.2()` in R) was selected as the best-fitting model. Colored symbols with horizontal error bars indicate effective LODs (with 95% confidence intervals) for different numbers of technical replicates (1 to 8 replicates). (**c**) Determination of the LOQ based on the exponential decay model. The $x$-axis represents copy numbers and the $y$-axis represents the coefficient of variation (CV) for copy number estimates calculated following Forootan et al. (2017) and Klymus et al. (2020). The blue curve indicates the exponential decay model (see Fig. S2 and Table S7 for comparisons of all candidate models). The red vertical line indicates the modeled LOD, and the black "*" symbol indicates the 35% CV precision threshold, at which the copy number is defined as the modeled LOQ (14 copies/reaction, equivalent to 7.0 copies/µL).
](formatted_figs/Fig03_StdCurve.pdf){width=100%}

</center>

![
**Figure S2 | Comparison of candidate models for determining the limit of quantification (LOQ) of the _Sousa chinensis_ qPCR assay.** (**a**)  Exponential decay, (**b**) linear, and (**c**–**g**) 2nd- to 6th-order polynomial models. The $x$-axis represents standard DNA concentrations (copies/reaction), and the $y$-axis represents the coefficient of variation (CV) for copy number estimates calculated following Forootan et al. (2017) and Klymus et al. (2020). Black points indicate observed CVs at each standard concentration ($n = 24$ replicates), and blue curves indicate the fitted models. Red vertical lines indicate the modeled LOD ($3.22$ copies/reaction), and black dotted lines indicate the 35% CV threshold (horizontal) and the resulting modeled LOQ (vertical). Model diagnostics ($\text{RSE}$, $\text{AIC}$, $\text{AICc}$, and $\text{BIC}$) for all seven models are provided in Table S7.  
](formatted_figs/FigS02_LOQAllModels.pdf){width=100%}

</center>

<center>

![
**Figure S5 | The relationship between seawater physical properties and qPCR detection in July 2024.** The relationship between qPCR detection of _Sousa chinensis_ eDNA and (**a**) the origin of water samples (surface or bottom), (**b**) temperature, (**c**) salinity, and (**d**) dissolved oxygen (DO), respectively. Red and blue colors indicate surface and bottom water samples, respectively. Lines in **b**-**d** indicate model predictions based on binomial GLMM with each sampling location as a random factor (`glmer(detection ~ environmental variable + (1 | location), family = binomial)`), although all the regressions are not statistically significant. Note that only qualitative results were used for this analysis because the eDNA concentrations of most samples were below the limit of quantification (LOQ).  
](formatted_figs/FigS05_SurveyqPCRxEnv.pdf){width=100%}

</center>
